text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 16 in history.
1272 - King Henry III of England, who had ruled since 1216, died and was succeeded by his son Edward I.
1797 - Frederick William II, king of Prussia from 1786, died and was succeeded by his son, Frederick William III.
1885 - Louis Riel, Canadian rebel leader who set up his own government, was hanged after being found guilty of treason.
1895 - Paul Hindemith, German composer and viola player, born. His music was banned by Hitler in 1933. He settled in the U.S. in 1939.
1896 - Oswald Mosley, British politician who formed the Union of Fascists, born. His provocative marches through the east end of London led to riots, and he was interned during World War Two.
1907 - Oklahoma became the 46th state of the Union.
1917 - Georges Clemenceau became prime minister of France for the second time.
1918 - After the break up of the Austro-Hungarian empire, Hungary was proclaimed an independent republic.
1933 - The U.S. and the Soviet Union established diplomatic relations.
1935 - France-Albert Rene, president of the Seychelles, born. Seized power in a bloodless coup in 1977 from pro-British president James Mancham.
1959 - The Rodgers & Hammerstein musical "The Sound of Music" premiered in New York, starring Mary Martin.
1960 - Clark Gable, American film actor and Oscar winner, died. Best known for his portrayal of Rhett Butler in "Gone with the Wind", he had just finished filming "The Misfits" with Marilyn Monroe.
1965 - William Cosgrave, Irish statesman and first president of the Irish Free State (1922-32), died.
1965 - The Soviet Union launched its Venus III spacecraft en route to Venus. It arrived in March, 1966, becoming the first spacecraft to land on another planet.
1973 - The U.S. launched Skylab 4, with three astronauts, on an 84-day mission.
1981 - William Holden (William Franklin Beedle), American actor who won an Oscar for "Stalag 17", died.
1989 - South African President F.W. de Klerk announced the scrapping of the Separate Amenities Act, opening up the country's beaches to all races.

1989 - Former East German leader Erich Honecker, his wife, and the ex-head of the secret police, Erich Mielke, were told by the Communist Party's new chief to give up their seats in parliament in an apparent purge.

1992 - A judicial inquiry dropped a political bombshell in South Africa, saying the army used a convicted murderer to recruit prostitutes and drug dealers to subvert Nelson Mandela's African National Congress.
1992 - In their first post-Soviet elections, Lithuania's Democratic Labour Party of ex-communists, won a crushing victory.
1994 - Jacques Medecin, former mayor of Nice, was extradited from Uruguay to France to face fraud and corruption charges.
1994 - Ukraine's parliament approved membership of the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty as a non-nuclear state but attached conditions to the document.
1995 - South Korea's former president Roh Tae-woo was arrested on charges of taking bribes.
1995 - U.N. tribunal charged Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic and his military commander Ratko Mladic with genocide.
1995 - A French court sentenced former communications minister Alain Carignon to three years in jail on corruption charges.
